baseline.session_basis: vendor says unknown; defaulted to bmo because 339 of 379 measured UK results announcements landed before 08:00 -- the resolver measures BOTH windows for this row
baseline.window: close of the session before 2026-10-12 -> 2026-10-12 close

options.reason: No European single-stock option chain is retrievable from a free source. Yahoo returns 0 expiries and 0 contracts for .L, .DE and .PA symbols against 21 and 196 for AAPL on the same crumb; Eurex's daily reference file carries trading parameters but no settlement prices, no open interest and no underlying ISIN map, and its statistics page is JavaScript with no JSON endpoint. So there is no event-implied move and no skew, and this baseline supplies its own priced_lean_pct and anchor_quality from the national short registers instead. This holds for all ten markets; nothing measured in 2026-09 on …

consensus.basis: Sell-side coverage, carried because it is the measurable proxy for this stage's thesis. Phase 1 measured 1-2 analysts below $1m/day of turnover, 5-7 at $1-5m, 11-13 at $5-25m and 16-19 above, consistently across all three markets. eu_resolve.py ranks the hunt BY this band so the thesis is tested rather than selected on.

history.caveat: Dates are REAL: each row is a results announcement the market's own archive records on that date, and the move is over this stage's own window. Only the UK (Investegate) and Norway (Oslo NewsWeb) reach this state; the other eight markets are estimated.

event_plausibility.basis: vendor forward calendar (TradingView), measured at a 2.2% phantom rate on 90 UK rows against the RNS record. Confirmation against Investegate (RNS mirror) is eu_resolve.py's job, after the fact.

positioning.basis: absent from a register that downloaded successfully, so no disclosed net short position at or above the 0.5% public threshold. A real zero -- but the threshold truncates, so 0.4% and 0.0% are both recorded here as 0.0, and the join is on the issuer NAME, so a name spelled differently in the register reads as a zero it should not.

expected_move.basis: the larger of (a) the median of this name's prior reactions and (b) a one-session move implied by 20-day realised volatility. It is NOT an option-implied move: nothing is paying for it and it carries no information about what the market expects from THIS print. It is a scale for how far this name travels. Phase 1 median realised move was 2.81% (UK), 3.12% (DE), 4.19% (FR) against Japan's 2.87%, with the tail intact in all three -- 42%, 27% and 52% maxima and no price limit to truncate them.

baseline.priced_lean_basis: Sum of the components above. Read eu_priced_in.lean_components(): every weight is a PRIOR borrowed from the US runs, none is measured on European data, and eu_resolve.py ranks each component separately so measurement can replace them. What matters is only that this is no longer identical to -0.05 * run_up_20d_pct, so the free control is a real rival again.

anchor_coverage.basis: `anchor_covered` is true only where the national short register returned a disclosed net short position for THIS issuer. A name the register was read for and does not name reads 0.0 -- real, but the 0.5% truncation floor rather than a measurement, and below $1m/day of turnover 168 of 190 sampled UK issuers read exactly that. The turnover floor moved from $1m to $200k on 2026-09-19, so this field is how the cost of that move is made visible: eu_resolve.py reports the Spearman split by it, with the count in each arm.

anchor_quality.basis: magnitude: realised vol plus a reaction history, capped at 0.5 because neither is an option-implied move, and cut to 0.35 where that history is a cadence estimate rather than observed dates -- measured 2026-09-22, an estimated history lands mostly on ordinary sessions and its median absolute move runs about half an observed one. direction: how many of the two positioning components resolved, capped at 0.45 because neither is 25-delta skew and Europe has no margin-balance component to add, and held to 0.15 where the register was read and does not name this issuer -- a truncated zero is not a di…

evidence.text: H1 FY27 profit is the one financial line not yet disclosed, and the pre-released mix (revenue +GBP3.1m, third-party manufacturing +19%, licensing +13% with accelerated income, ~GBP1m annualised central savings completed in H2 FY26) points to adjusted PBT above H1 FY26's GBP2.2m, but it lands inside the reiterated GBP6.5m FY guide and the footnote that GBP3.6m of the GBP4.9m licensing is accelerated IFRS 15 income invites a quality-of-earnings discount.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Interim results days: +2.36% (Oct 2023), -16.34% (Oct 2024), +3.16% (Oct 2025); the H1 trading update this year moved +1.94%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Revenue and the FY guide are priced (stock 79p on the update, 75p now); the H1 profit number itself has never been published and the stock has 1 analyst and ~$100k/day turnover. If the market expected a strong H1 profit the shares would not sit at an 11% discount to NTA after an in-line update; equally the accelerated-licensing caveat is why this stays small.
evidence.independence: Prior interim: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/sanderson-design-group--sdg/half-year-results/9171299 (H1 FY26 adj PBT GBP2.2m, GBP1m overhead cut completed) -- same issuer, different document.

evidence.text: The board pulled the interims forward nine days, from Wednesday 21 October (set in the 7 August RNS) to Monday 12 October, two weeks after a 14% holder requisitioned a GM to remove the chair -- a board defending itself has every incentive to front-load the strongest possible results, outlook and shareholder-return message before its circular.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior date change or contested GM at SDG on record in the Investegate history (751 RNS back to before 2023).
evidence.why_not_priced: The stock was flat at 74.5p on the 8 October notice and on the requisition (73p); the domestic coverage (ii.co.uk, 29 Sep) still lists 21 October, so the move has not been read alongside the requisition. If priced, one would expect a run-up into the date; 5d run-up is +0.67%.
evidence.independence: Requisition RNS 2026-09-28 https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/sanderson-design-group--sdg/general-meeting-requisition-notice/9792825 and the original 21 Oct date in https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/sanderson-design-group--sdg/half-year-trading-update-/9709634 -- the inference joins two documents, nothing states the motive.

evidence.text: Closest listed peer Colefax reported fabric sales to 18 September 2026 with US +14.0% and UK -4.5%, consistent with SDG's H1 shape and pointing to continued US strength in SDG's first H2 weeks.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: SDG's last current-trading lines: H1 TU +1.94%, FY TU Feb 2026 +16.67%, Jan 2025 TU -12.04% -- current trading drives this name.
evidence.why_not_priced: A peer read-through on a one-analyst name; SDG did not move on the Colefax statement. Proxy only, and Colefax is 66% US against SDG's ~37% NA brand share, so transmission is partial and SDG's larger UK exposure (-8% in H1) offsets it.
evidence.independence: SDG's own H1 TU states 'trading has been excellent with a clear upward trend' in the US: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/sanderson-design-group--sdg/half-year-trading-update-/9709634

evidence.text: The Designers Guild licence (sole worldwide rights, manufactured at Anstey and Lancaster, immediate replenishment of best-sellers) is the first incremental brand volume since the period end and the interims are the first chance to quantify it or fold it into the outlook.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Announced 2026-09-25 15:54; stock 73.0p -> 73.2p that day: no reaction.
evidence.why_not_priced: Announced without numbers and ignored by the price; the operating company is in administration so the old revenue base is unknown to the market. Small because it is public, royalty-bearing and starts with stock-build costs, so an FY27 upgrade on it is unlikely this early.
evidence.independence: Business of Home 2026-09-25 (Designers Guild in administration, Osborne & Little kept as US distributor): https://businessofhome.com/articles/sanderson-to-revive-designers-guild-brand
